reasoning: Both sets share the same scaffolding: a single package, an interface task in Phase 0, spines, wiring and a system phase, with similar task granularity and packet format. B has the stronger content. Its spec turns each stage into an explicit RL lesson: a tabular → DQN → CNN ladder with ablations for Snake, REINFORCE vs PPO tested head to head on one fish, and fixed opponents → naive co-learning → opponent-pool self-play for predator-prey. It also gives a one-to-one mapping to the reference library. Its golden cases have concrete numbers, and the ones I checked hold: reflection, swim scaling, GAE 1.3775, the compact-view bits, the catch distances in TC-52 and TC-58, and the tail-cell move. B's flaws are real but local. The brief still says 'Not doing: designing future environments now'. The CONSTRAINTS boundaries leave out `selfplay` and `viz`'s dependencies. TC-46 contradicts EVAL-07. `gae`'s contract disagrees with TC-42 on the length of `values`. Each stage is one large milestone. A splits the fish stage more finely, into one fish → many fish → local sight, and has a careful statistical protocol. But A's tests.md was not updated after spec changes. TC-07 and TC-25 score the fish by 'hits per fish, lower is better' while FISH-04 says mean survival steps, higher is better. TC-08 assumes hit fish respawn. TC-09 has 2 predators while the spec has 1. TC-24 allows a 90-minute batch against QR-02's 60 minutes. The roadmap's M3 and M4 exit criteria cite those stale cases. A's M1 also can't replay the trained snake, though watching a replay is part of the stage's success. Its M2 bundles the DQN upgrade, the viewer, video, the reference check and the write-up. Its task IDs run out of order, and one edge in its dependency graph is a false serialization. On balance, B wins narrowly.

strengths: Precise EVAL-04 statistical protocol (paired permutation, Holm, per-run rule check)
Fish stage split into one/many/local-sight milestones, each with checkable Exit
Clear seed ranges, determinism digest, and check-world gate (AD-09) with a two-exit corridor that a learner biased to one action can't pass
Packets include spec requirement text alongside contract sections
weaknesses: tests.md stale against spec for fish and predator-prey (score definition, respawn, predator count)
M1 delivers no replay of the trained snake; M2 is a grab-bag of viewer, video, reference check, write-up and DQN tuning
Task IDs out of order in plan (T13 after T15, T25/T26 before T24)
Less explicit RL pedagogy: no ablations and no REINFORCE-vs-PPO comparison claim

strengths: Each stage built as a concept ladder with ablations and tested comparisons (PPO > REINFORCE, rung 3 > rung 2)
Golden cases with exact, hand-checkable numbers derived from the spec examples
Teams and batch-first core designed up front, so later stages don't rewrite M1
Reference mapping pinned one-to-one, with SB3 defaults documented
weaknesses: Brief stale: 'Not doing: Designing future environments now' while S2/S3 are fully specced
CONSTRAINTS boundaries omit selfplay and viz→evaluate
One milestone per stage makes M1 very large; spines are mostly full implementations
TC-46 contradicts EVAL-07 on which rungs must beat the scripted fish
